title: Writing for Television and Film
description: Theory and practice in writing for electronic and film media. Introduction to techniques of narrative and documentary writing and scripting.

title: Cinema as Art
description: Cinema in its diverse forms. Historical and stylistic influences on aesthetic values and social implications of cinema.

title: The Art of Creating Emotion in Movies
description: Film production for non-majors. Ways filmmakers deploy formal elements of cinema to generate a genre-related emotion such as fear in the horror genre; love in the romance genre.

title: Cinema in Africa
description: Filmmaking in sub-Saharan Africa after colonization.

title: Independent Cinema
description: Filmmaking that has declared independence from mainstream aesthetics, industrial conventions, and the political status quo.

title: Introduction to Filmmaking
description: An introduction to the roles, techniques, and concepts of film production, including producing, directing, cinematography, sound, and post-production. Course includes hands-on learning designed for students of all skill levels.

title: Film, Television, and New Media Criticism
description: Critical approaches to study of film, television, and new media. Analyses of media perspectives, to include ideology, semiotics, genre, gender, and spectatorship.

title: Film and Video Production
description: Aesthetics and practice of film and video production techniques. Instruction in equipment use combined with consideration of aesthetics, visual storytelling, and craft. Attention to development of creative voice and original work.

title: Sound Design for Video and Film
description: Digital audio post-production for video, TV, and film. Includes field acquisition, Foley, editing, and assembling.

title: Cinematography for Television and Film
description: Basic cinematography to include introduction to filmmaking activities, lighting techniques for film and television, specialized studio and location equipment. Exhibitions to include broadcasts, film festivals, and special screenings.

title: Film and Video Editing
description: Theory and practice of film and video editing.

title: Cultural Aspects of Media
description: Cultural dimensions of media. Media structures, uses, and effects at national and international levels in a context of humanities and conceptual arts.

title: Intermediate Documentary
description: This intermediate documentary film production workshop will provide an introduction to the building blocks of nonfiction filmmaking. The workshop combines theory, history and practice. You will gain production experience working individually and in groups.

title: Staging and Art for Television and Film
description: Aesthetic considerations and technical practices in staging, lighting, and graphics for television and film. Practical experience in university sponsored productions.

title: Studio Production
description: Multi-camera television production techniques for studio, sound stage, and remote multi-camera production. Responsibilities of producer, director, and production staff.

title: Intermediate Filmmaking
description: Single camera techniques in production of narrative fiction. Crew-based location and studio production. Responsibilities of producer, director, and key creative production positions.

title: International Cinema
description: Construction of foreign film to history and practice of cinema as an art. Film as an expression of national culture.

title: History of Film Classics: Early Developments Through the 1950s
description: Viewing and analysis of American and foreign theatrical films which represent milestones in development of cinema.

title: History of Film Classics: 1960s Through Today’s Cinema
description: Viewing and analysis of American and foreign theatrical films which represent milestones in development of cinema.

title: Professional Writing for Film and Television
description: Professional writing for film and television production, publicity, criticism, and commentary.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C (2.0) or better. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Business Aspects of Television and Film Production
description: Financing, preproduction planning, postproduction, and distribution of television and film.

title: Intermediate Screenwriting and Script Analysis
description: The study of film narrative through story analysis and the craft of screenwriting. Emphasis on designing narrative, characters, dialogue, genre, and tone.

title: History of Television
description: Critical survey of television history, from its origins in radio and film, to its contemporary convergence with digital media and the internet. Topics include regulation, media ownership, technology, aesthetics, genre, authorship, advertising, and audiences, with a focus on sociocultural issues.

title: Compositing and Visual Effects
description: Computer-generated visual effects to include rendering and compositing techniques used in film, new media, and television.

title: Critical Studies of Gender/Sexuality/Media
description: Critical approaches to representation, production, and reception of gender and sexuality in film, television and new media, including video games and the Internet.

title: Internship
description: Work with approved agencies off-campus under the combined supervision of agency personnel and instructor.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Experimental topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study or project, normally in a research area selected by the student.

title: Advanced Film Distribution and Marketing
description: Exposure to the inner workings of industry standard film distribution and marketing strategies, processes, and techniques; advanced knowledge and skills to tactically release indie films to audiences worldwide.

title: Advanced Script Writing for Television and Film
description: Scripting of dramatic original and adaptation forms, and documentary.

title: Television Writing and the Dynamics of the Writers’ Room
description: Scripting of spec and original material for television. Attention to learning fundamentals of managing and running the television writers’ room.

title: Advanced Sound Design for Film and Interactive Media
description: Aesthetics and advanced techniques for designing sounds for moving image and interactive media. Through laboratories and projects, students will learn auralization, composition, design, and synthesis using contemporary tools: audio programming languages, digital audio workstations, and nonlinear editors.

title: Advanced Film and Television Cinematography
description: Art, craft, and industry of cinematography. Telling visual stories with video and film. Attributes and optics of lenses. Qualities and aesthetics of lighting.

title: Selected Topics in Genre Studies for Television and Film
description: Film and television genres (noir, western, comedy, musical, science fiction, soap opera, etc.) including key media texts, aesthetics, themes, history, and social context.

title: Documentary Production
description: Hands-on field experiences in documentary production to include research and writing techniques, investigative procedures, interviewing, shooting and editing. Analyze significant documentaries.

title: Art Direction for Television and Film
description: Aesthetic, technical, and practical aspects of design for television and film. Experience in scenic design, graphics, set decoration, budgeting, and scheduling.

title: Production Design for Television and Film
description: Theory and analysis of production design concepts for television and film. Development of designs and analysis of technical requirements for fictional and nonfictional productions.

title: 3D Digital Storytelling
description: Narrative in animation. Pre-production and production techniques in 3D animated film.

title: Costume Design for Television and Film
description: Advanced studies in costume design. Budgeting and departmental management, character development, design problems, materials, production, rendering layout, script breakdowns.

title: Digital Design for Film and Stage
description: Theories and applications of commonly used 3D modeling programs in the entertainment industry.

title: Advanced Film
description: Practicum in direction and production of dramatic and nondramatic film. Cameras, lighting, design, sound techniques, experience in university sponsored productions. Completion of a short film.

title: Advanced Television
description: Production processes and techniques to include producing, critical analysis, directing, digital cinematography, and editing of scripted projects. Experience in individual and university-sponsored productions.

title: Doomsday Cinema
description: Explores the theme of “Doomsday”, on television, cinema, and videogames. Students will create their own doomsday scenarios based on real-life events like climate change, pandemics, AI, and nuclear threats. It includes studying various media, texts, and prophecies to inspire their creations, culminating in ready for film projects, final treatments and synopses.

title: Documentary: History and Theory
description: Persuasive concepts, techniques, and forms in documentary film. Major historical works and their impact on society.

title: Selected Topics in Director Studies
description: Historical significance of and theoretical approaches to major media directors (Welles, Hitchcock, Spielberg, etc.) including breadth of work, cultural and generic contexts, aesthetic innovation, and recurring themes.

title: Selected Topics in History of Film, TV, and Media
description: Media history including cultural and generic developments, patterns of exhibition, technological influences, significant creative and industrial figures, commercial and social contexts.

title: Directing for Film and Television
description: Directing fundamentals and production to include script analysis, director’s preparation and directing actors.

title: Selected Topics in Television, Film and New Media
description: Specialized study of selected topics from the areas of television, film and new media.

title: Business Aspects of Film
description: Business aspects of independent film production to include television and Internet streaming. Culture and practices of the film industry in context of career development.

title: Seminar: Production for Television and Film
description: Film and television production. Lectures and production of two short media projects that link research to artistic process and familiarize students with all aspects of the television, film and new media program.

title: Seminar: Intensive Television and Film
description: Intensive seminar in cinematography, direction, editing, and sound production for television and film. Tools of production culminating in the presentation and critique of students’ creative work.

title: Seminar in Writing for Television and Film
description: Non-dramatic and dramatic structures as they apply to non-fiction and fiction television programs and films. Writing full length script or scenario.

title: Seminar in Writing for New Media
description: Narrative and non-narrative writing for new media to include gaming, interactive media, social media, and transmedia formats.

title: Sound Design for Film
description: Digital audio production for film, to include automated dialog replacement (ADR), field acquisition, Foley, mixing, sound editing, sweetening.

title: Fundamentals of Cinematography
description: Hands-on overview of the art and craft of motion picture photography. To include study of camera, lenses, and lighting. Introduction to various leadership roles in cinematography.

title: Seminar: Writing Short Narrative and Documentary Films
description: Creating scripts for short narrative films and documentary productions.

title: Film Editing and Postproduction
description: Theory and practice of film editing to include color grading, digital post-production workflow, sound and picture cutting.

title: Scene-Based Film Production
description: Single camera techniques in production of narrative fiction to include scene construction and production roles. Crew-based location and studio production.

title: Seminar: Midway Review Production
description: Development and completion of midway project for presentation before faculty jury. Research, presentation and analysis of related work, and creative engagement with material and subject matter to include retrospective written analysis of the work.

title: Seminar: Research and Bibliography in Media Production
description: Methods of research, critical analysis, and writing in relation to creative work.

title: Portfolio/Examination Preparation
description: Supervised preparation for portfolio review and oral defense.

title: MFA Capstone Project
description: Preparation of a capstone project for the M.F.A. Plan B option.

title: Capstone Public Presentation
description: Presentation based on written thesis to include a problem in history, theory, or pedagogy showing evidence of original research (M.F.A. Plan A); presentation of creative work developed in M.F.A. Capstone Project (MFA Plan B).

title: MFA Research
description: Research in preparation for the thesis or capstone project.

title: Special Study
description: Contract required. Arranged with graduate coordinator in area of study.

title: Thesis or Project
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis or Project Extension
description: Following assignment of RP in Course 799A, registration in this course is required in any semester in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in this course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.
